key_provisions_or_claims: Intelligent robot crimes fall into three types: program malfunction, use by natural persons, and external malicious interference.
Out-of-control robot programs blur the identification of criminal liability subjects and complicate causation and culpability.
For design, clarify the relationship between harmful, criminal and implementation behaviour.
For testing and certification, apply conditional (but-for) and objective attribution theories to assign responsibility.
Strengthen foresight and safe-use obligations for users and regulators, and improve criminal liability rules for testers and certifiers.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article on criminal law regulation of crimes caused by out-of-control intelligent robot programs. It analyses blurred liability subjects and proposes criminal-law measures across design, testing and certification, and use and regulation, applying conditional and objective attribution theories and foresight obligations.
annotation.title_clean: Research on the Criminal Law Regulation of Crimes Caused by Out-of-Control Intelligent Robot Programs
